Microsoft Reports $10 Billion in Quarterly Revenue Linked to Commercial Arrangements With OpenAI

30 Oct 2026, 04:19 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Tech Desk · Source: techcrunch.com

Image: Rebecca Bellan — Creative Commons

Key takeaways Financial Ties Revealed in Regulatory Filing Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from its commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, during the quarter that ended on September 30, 2026. According to a regulatory filing released by

Financial Ties Revealed in Regulatory Filing

Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from its commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, during the quarter that ended on September 30, 2026. According to a regulatory filing released by Microsoft, this figure accounts for nearly 11% of the company's total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion.

The figures underscore the substantial financial relationship between the two entities, even as they increasingly compete for overlapping customer bases. Because Microsoft's fiscal year begins in July, the quarter ending in September marked the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal year. For the full 2026 fiscal year, Microsoft's revenue from OpenAI reached $24.1 billion. Based on the latest quarterly trajectory, Microsoft's annual revenue from OpenAI-related arrangements could approach $40 billion.

Outstanding Receivables and Evolving Agreements

In addition to recognized revenue, Microsoft reported $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI at the end of September, rising from $6 billion at the close of June. This balance reflects amounts owed by OpenAI for prior transactions rather than newly generated revenue.

The exact breakdown of how much of Microsoft's revenue stems from Azure cloud computing services versus revenue-sharing payments remains undisclosed in official filings. Previous reports and industry arrangements indicate that OpenAI historically agreed to share a portion of its revenue with Microsoft following early investments exceeding $13 billion, though neither company has publicly confirmed the exact percentage. Under an agreement reached in April 2026, OpenAI is slated to continue sharing revenue with Microsoft through 2030, subject to an established cap, while retaining the freedom to collaborate with competing cloud providers.

Structural Shifts and Partnership Evolution

The partnership structures have evolved since October 2025, when Microsoft relinquished its exclusive hold on OpenAI, permitting the startup to partner with alternative cloud providers. In exchange, OpenAI committed to purchasing an additional $250 billion in Azure services. Meanwhile, Microsoft’s equity stake in OpenAI has shifted from approximately 25% in June to 24% in September, continuing a gradual dilution from roughly 27% following an October 2025 recapitalization. Microsoft has not detailed the specific causes of this dilution.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers and industry analysts tracking the financial health of the artificial intelligence sector can review corporate regulatory filings directly through investor relations portals. While these figures demonstrate significant cash flow and service commitments between Microsoft and OpenAI, observers should note the distinction between recognized revenue and outstanding receivables when evaluating commercial dependency.

To verify the original reporting and examine the official disclosures, readers can consult the coverage on [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/28/microsoft-recorded-10-billion-in-revenue-from-openai/).
